chinatown.name: Chinatown
chinatown.title: Explore Chinatown in Singapore: Top Things to Do

tiles.title: Chinatown Heritage Centre
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eStep back in time at Chinatown Heritage Centre, rebuilt from memories of early residents who lived in these shophouses. Immerse in their stories of struggles and dreams.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Smith Street
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eExperience Smith Street, where Chinatown\u0027s heritage meets modern energy through traditional shops, eateries, creative spaces, and cultural activities that bring traditions to life.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Chinatown Murders (牛车水 Murders)
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eThis murder mystery tour through Chinatown is filled with intriguing clues and untold stories.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Trails of Tan Ah Huat
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eHop on a bicycle and let Tan Ah Huat – a fictitious coolie – bring the streets of Chinatown to life.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Growing Up - A Mural Walk in Chinatown
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDiscover Chinatown\u0027s past with an art walk featuring murals by Yip Yew Chong. Don’t forget to snap away!\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Buddha Tooth Relic Temple \u0026 Museum
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eHome to a sacred relic, this majestic temple is a trove of Buddhist wisdom.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Masjid Jamae
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eOne of our city\u0027s oldest mosques, Masjid Jamae is famous for its eastern and western infused architecture.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Sri Mariamman Temple
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eStep into Singapore’s oldest Hindu temple to admire the ornate carvings and soak in the vibrant atmosphere.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Thian Hock Keng Temple
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eSingapore’s oldest Chinese temple is steeped in heritage and\u0026nbsp;is a must-visit for history aficionados.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Singapore Art Museum
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eSingapore\u0027s pioneering art museum is home to the work of bright young artists and regional names alike.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Chinatown Street Market
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eMore than just a shopping stretch, this iconic street is home to a wide range of offerings, from lacquered fans to charming souvenirs.\u003cbr\u003e\r \u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Yue Hwa Building
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eGo treasure hunting in Yue Hwa building – this charming department store is chock full of anything you\u0027d desire, from traditional herbs and calligraphy brushes to tasty snacks.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Bee Cheng Hiang
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eWith humble street hawker roots that date back to the 1930s, Bee Cheng Hiang serves up delicious slices of freshly barbecued meat.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Kele
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eStarting out as a humble bakery nearly four decades ago, Kele is now one of Singapore\u0027s most popular snack brands. Sample their pineapple tarts and savour the tradition!\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Pek Sin Choon
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eTalk about an old-school pick me up. Pek Sin Choon has been selling its range of fragrant, traditional tea for almost a century.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: On Cheong Jewellery
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eFrom jade bangles and gold necklaces to beautifully-crafted rings, this traditional jeweller boasts a range of masterful designs.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Binary Style
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eShop from a homegrown lifestyle brand, renowned for its vibrant prints inspired by local architecture and nature.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Chop Wah On
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eSoothe your aches at Chop Wah On, one of Singapore\u0027s oldest medicated oil makers. Since 1916, this family business crafts healing remedies and traditional balms.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Eu Yan Sang
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eExperience traditional wellness at Eu Yan Sang, a trusted name in Chinese medicine for over 145 years. Discover time-tested herbal remedies and wellness products.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Chinatown Complex
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eEat your way through the delectable dishes at Chinatown Complex, Singapore\u0027s largest food centre. Keep your eye out for the Michelin Bib Gourmand-awarded hawker stalls!\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Maxwell Food Centre
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eA beloved stomping ground of local foodies, Maxwell Food Centre is home to hawker delights like chicken rice.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: No Sleep Club
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eRanked 15 on 2023\u0027s list of Asia\u0027s 50 Best Bars, No Sleep Club is the perfect spot for coffee, cocktails or bar food with an elevated twist.\u003cbr\u003e\r \u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Zen
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eBjorn Frantzén\u0027s three Michelin-starred restaurant is famed for its masterful take on Scandinavian and Japanese fusion cuisine.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Native
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eSample the flavours of Asia at one of Asia\u0027s 50 Best Bars – the unique cocktails here are concocted with ingredients and spirits from Singapore and across the region.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Tong Heng Traditional Cantonese Pastries
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eSome of the toothsome pastries from Tong Heng include candied melon pastries, savoury buns and their signature egg tarts.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Kok Sen Restaurant
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eThis Michelin Bib Gourmand-awarded restaurant is run by the\u0026nbsp;third generation and serves up a tantalising range of Cantonese cuisine.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Restaurant Espoir
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eRestaurant Espoir blends European culinary artistry with bold flavours of Malayan herbs and spices, offering a modern Halal dining experience with delightful surprises in every bite.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Clan Hotel
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eModern luxury meets old-school heritage in the heart of Chinatown, with Clan Hotel\u0027s immaculate service and well-appointed rooms.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: PARKROYAL COLLECTION Pickering, Singapore
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eBesides exquisite amenities and world-class hospitality, PARKROYAL COLLECTION Pickering, Singapore is famed for its award-winning designs for sustainability.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 30
tiles.description: Skyscrapers and colonial buildings sit side by side in the Civic District, home to some of the island's finest museums and art galleries.

tiles.title: Highlight 31
tiles.description: Discover things to do in the Dempsey enclave, which covers the Dempsey, Minden, and Loewen clusters. Our guide covers unique shopping spots and what to eat at restaurants on Dempsey.

tiles.title: Highlight 32
tiles.description: Timeless tradition and bold new cultures come together on the streets of Kampong Gelam, where street art and trendy hangouts sit alongside traditional landmarks.

tiles.title: Highlight 33
tiles.description: Home to Peranakan culture in Singapore, Katong-Joo Chiat is filled with local flavours, boutique cafes, and charming heritage shophouses.

tiles.title: Highlight 34
tiles.description: Walk the streets of Little India, and discover a harmonious blend of age-old tradition, cutting edge architecture and shops selling traditional garments and intricate jewellery.

tiles.title: Highlight 35
tiles.description: Ignite your love for nature with the majestic animals, nature-themed attractions and lush greenery at Mandai.

tiles.title: Highlight 36
tiles.description: With its soaring skyscrapers and gorgeous skyline, the Marina Bay we see today is made up of 38 hectares of reclaimed land.

tiles.title: Highlight 37
tiles.description: Orchard Road is the beating heart of Singapore. From luxury shopping to subculture hangouts, there’s a new surprise waiting for you at every corner. Go where your heart takes you and experience the hottest attractions around. Or, take a look at our curated itineraries to find your place in Singapore’s busiest and most iconic street.

tiles.title: Highlight 38
tiles.description: Endless discovery awaits you with Sentosa's golden beaches, tranquil getaways and thrilling theme parks.

tiles.title: Highlight 39
tiles.description: From delectable food to buzzing nightlife, the Singapore River's trio of quays are bound to deliver a wave of exciting experiences.

contentLines: Buddha Tooth Relic Temple & Museum in Singapore
Buddha Tooth Relic Temple & Museum

Built in 2007, the temple gets its name from what the Buddhists regard as the left canine tooth of Buddha, which has been recovered from his funeral pyre in Kushinagar, India and displayed on the temple’s grounds. The Buddha Tooth Relic is housed in a giant stupa made from 320 kilograms of gold.

This Tang-styled Chinese Buddhist temple costs S$75 million to set up, and is based on various elements of Tang Dynasty architecture. The building’s design was inspired by the Buddhist Mandala, a symbol of Buddhist culture that represents the universe.

More than just a place of worship, Buddha Tooth Relic Temple is also home to two museums, with fascinating stories about figures of note in the tradition, as well as the sacred relics of the Buddha and his disciples.

contentLines: Sri Mariamman Hindu Temple Singapore | Chinatown Landmark

From the ornate exterior adorned with carvings of Hindu deities, to the exquisite ceiling paintings in its main hall, its majestic grand tower entrance features five tiers of sculptures of deities and mythological figures. Sri Mariamman Temple is a beautiful spot for a photo and is a landmark for generations of Hindu worshippers and Singaporeans alike.
Immerse in Local Festivities
More than just a historical landmark, the temple is a bustling place of worship, with sacred festivals like the firewalking festival, Theemithi, held annually.
Experience Vibrant Hindu Traditions
With shrines dedicated to gods and heroes from Hinduism, this place of worship is a great place to learn about the religion's rich traditions.

contentLines: Jamae Mosque (Masjid Chulia) | Historic Gem in Singapore
Masjid Jamae (Masjid Chulia)

With a history that dates all the way back to 1826, this mosque is a must-visit for history buffs. Masjid Jamae was the first of three mosques in Chinatown erected by the Chulias, who were Tamil Muslims from the Coromandel Coast of Southern India.

Masjid Jamae's beautiful architecture blends eclectic traditions, from Indian and Islamic styles to western and Greek influences. The entrance gate has a South Indian Indo-Islamic influence, while the prayer hall’s neoclassical features include Doric columns and large windows with Chinese green-glazed tiles.
Besides being a beautiful building, the mosque also organizes classes occasionally. Be sure to check their website for opportunities to participate in seminars, tours and discussions.

A hotspot of cultural activity, Chinatown Street Market gets even more vibrant during traditional festivals like Chinese New Year and Mid-Autumn Festival.
This bustling stretch is home to eateries and restaurants serving up a variety of delicious local food including chicken rice, popiah and chendol.

tiles.title: Sultan Mosque
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eAn iconic architectural landmark, the impressive\u0026nbsp;Sultan Mosque is a focal point for Singapore’s Muslim community.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Hajjah Fatimah Mosque
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eAlso known as Masjid Hajjah Fatimah, the Hajjah Fatimah Mosque will captivate you with its blend of cross-cultural architectural influences.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: #instawalk: Bugis, Waterloo, Kampong Gelam
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eTake a jaunt around Bugis, Waterloo Street and Kampong Gelam, explore hidden gems and snap a trove of Instagram-worthy shots for your social media feeds.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Haji Lane
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eSingapore\u0027s original indie neighbourhood is a great place to wander, with its hole-in-the-wall bars, boutique fashion stores and indie businesses. Keep a look out for wall murals and graffiti by both local and internationally-renowned artists.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: A Painted Sip
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eA beginner-friendly immersive painting workshop where participants can paint and customise their own reusable tumblers and choose from a range of Singapore-inspired designs.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Kebaya by Ratianah
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eMasterfully-tailored from exquisite fabric, the \u003ci\u003ekebaya\u003c/i\u003e and the \u003ci\u003ebaju kurung\u003c/i\u003e from Ratianah Tahir\u0027s boutique are bound to brighten up your wardrobe.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Jamal Kazura Aromatics
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eFall in love with the world of perfume at Jamal Kazura Aromatics, a traditional perfumery that\u0027s been around since 1933. Discover a perfume that speaks to your personality or create your own signature scent.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Hygge
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eClassical designs and elegant minimalism exude from the trinkets, accessories and decor on display at Hygge. Take home a dose of cosiness, and find the ideal gift for your loved ones at home.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Crafune
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eGet inspired to work with your hands, and pick up basics of leather-working at Crafune, where you can learn how to make your very own accessories, from wallets to handbags.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Bugis Street
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eA bustling street market that sells everything from quirky knick knacks to fashionable garments. Scour the best deals through shops packed with clothes, shoes and accessories.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Goodluck Bunch
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eIf you\u0027re a fan of street culture, you\u0027re going to love the effortlessly cool vibes at Goodluck Bunch, with its selection of hoodies, sneakers and apparel for both men and women.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Toko Aljunied
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eIntricate\u0026nbsp;\u003ci\u003ebatik\u0026nbsp;\u003c/i\u003efabrics and gorgeous, hand-sewn garments are on display at this traditional store, with a history that dates all the way back to 1940.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Hjh Maimunah
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDig into food that tastes just like your \u003ci\u003emakcik\u003c/i\u003e (aunty) made it at Hjh Maimunah. This Michelin Bib Gourmand eatery is famous for its \u003ci\u003enasi padang\u003c/i\u003e – rice with an assortment of delicious side dishes, from beef \u003ci\u003erendang\u003c/i\u003e to \u003ci\u003esambal \u003c/i\u003eprawns.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Rumah Makan Minang
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eRun by the third generation, the rich and diverse flavours of Indonesian cuisine are on full display at Rumah Makan Minang. Enjoy delicious traditional fare like\u0026nbsp;\u003ci\u003etahu telur\u0026nbsp;\u003c/i\u003eand\u0026nbsp;\u003ci\u003emee soto.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/i\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: The Coconut Club
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDig into a plate of\u0026nbsp;\u003ci\u003enasi lemak\u0026nbsp;\u003c/i\u003e– a traditional rice dish made with a variety of side ingredients. The version whipped up by The Coconut Club, a Michelin Bib Gourmand recipient, elevates this hawker staple with a modern spin on its ingredients.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Bar Stories
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eThis cozy\u0026nbsp;watering hole offers bespoke cocktails to thirsty tipplers, with a variety of drinks inspired by your response to the bartenders\u0027 questions.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Ji Xiang Ang Ku Kueh
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eJi Xiang is a local brand that specializes in Ang Ku Kueh, a traditional Chinese pastry made with soft and chewy glutinous rice flour. Located right opposite Bugis Junction, this store is one of its 10 outlets in Singapore.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Lou Shang
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eLou Shang, which means \u0026quot;upstairs\u0026quot; in English, is a cafe that offers a trip down memory lane through its nostalgic decor and locally inspired menu. It is located at Prinsep Street in the Bras Basah and Bugis precinct.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Bugis HaveFun LiveShow
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eImmerse yourself in the electrifying atmosphere at HaveFun Live Show at Bugis+. Enjoy an unforgettable night with bar delights and close-up live performances!\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: The Sultan
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eAdmire the columns and full-length shuttered French windows of the conserved buildings that houses The Sultan, and then step inside to immerse yourself in a world of comfort.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Andaz Singapore
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eTreat yourself to thoughtfully designed guestrooms with stunning views of the city, at the first Andaz-branded property in Southeast Asia.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 23

tiles.title: Highlight 24

tiles.title: Highlight 27

tiles.title: Highlight 28

Go where your heart takes you and experience the hottest attractions around. Or, take a look at our curated itineraries to find your place in Singapore’s busiest and most iconic street.

tiles.title: Highlight 30
tiles.description: Endless discovery awaits you with Sentosa's golden beaches, tranquil getaways and thrilling theme parks.

tiles.title: Highlight 31
tiles.description: From delectable food to buzzing nightlife, the Singapore River's trio of quays are bound to deliver a wave of exciting experiences.

tiles.title: Highlight 3
tiles.description: Experience the serenity and learn the history of Hajjah Fatimah Mosque in Singapore. Discover the religious and architectural significance of the mosque today!

contentLines: Sultan Mosque (Masjid) Singapore | Kampong Gelam Landmark
Striking Architecture Abounds

The mosque's distinctive golden domes are adorned with glass bottle ends at the base of the structure, which were collected and donated by the lower-income as their contributions to the mosque’s construction. Winner of the prestigious Architectural Award in 2016, the mosque's golden dome is so iconic, towering over nearby shophouses.
A Glimpse into the Muslim Faith
Built in 1824 by Sultan Hussein Shah, the first Sultan of Singapore, the mosque is a vibrant symbol of the Muslim faith, and a focal point of Singapore's Malay community.
A Place to Expand One's Horizons
The mosque welcomes visitors to explore the compound on a guided tour or a free walk.

katong-joo-chiat.title: Katong-Joo Chiat: Home of Singapore's Peranakan Houses

tiles.title: The Intan
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eOwner and curator Alvin Yapp has transformed his home into a museum dedicated to the Peranakan culture, with a hoard of fascinating artefacts.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Eurasian Heritage Gallery
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eLearn about the history of the Eurasian community in Singapore across the three galleries of this quaint heritage attraction.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Colourful Shophouses along Koon Seng Road
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eSnap a shot for Instagram at these iconic, pastel-hued houses. Fun fact: they date back to the 1920s and were inhabited by a diverse community, including the Peranakan Chinese.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Katong Antique House
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eThe private museum is a trove of Peranakan antiques ranging from furniture to intricately crafted \u003ci\u003eNyonya\u003c/i\u003e costumes like \u003ci\u003esarong kebaya\u003c/i\u003e and \u003ci\u003ekasut-manek\u003c/i\u003e (beaded shoes).\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Katong-Joo Chiat - Nyonyas, Babas and Peranakan Tour
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDiscover the old-school architecture, charming shophouses and bustling atmosphere of the neighbourhood from the sidecar of a vintage Vespa.\u003c/p\u003e\r
tiles.image: https://www.visitsingapore.com/content/dam/visitsingapore/neighbourhoods/katong-joo-chiat/updated/title-slider/Joo Chiat + Katong - Nyonyas, Babas and Peranakan_Option 1_Source Singapore Sidecars-544x544.jpg

tiles.title: Sri Senpaga Vinayagar Temple
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eOne of the oldest Hindu temples in Singapore, its four granite pillars, etched entrance stone, and unique musical pillar offers visitors a captivating journey through centuries of tradition and devotion.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Cat Socrates
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eBrowse through a host of books and knick-knacks at this cool indie retail shop,\u0026nbsp;Cat Socrates—and say hi to the resident cats!\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Kim Choo Kueh Chang
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eFrom delicious \u003ci\u003eNyonya\u003c/i\u003e \u003ci\u003ekueh\u003c/i\u003e and dumplings to exquisite dresses and jewellery, this beloved store has been selling all things Peranakan since 1945.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Hat of Cain
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eGet dapper and show off your style at Hat of Cain, which specialises in authentic, handwoven hats from Ecuador for both men and women.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Onlewo
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eTake home a piece of Singapore with you. The trinkets, gifts\u0026nbsp;and home-decor items from Onlewo are inspired by iconic local neighbourhoods, wildlife and motifs.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Rumah Bebe
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eLearn the intricacies of Peranakan beadwork or peruse a selection of finely crafted wares at this colourful establishment.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Quentin\u0027s Eurasian Restaurant
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDig into comfort food with an Eurasian twist at this beloved\u0026nbsp;restaurant. From hearty corned beef rice and fried okra to fiery curry debal (or devil curry), the dishes here are bound to sate your appetite.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Kway Guan Huat Joo Chiat Popiah
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eLearn how the beloved local dish popiah is made at this eight-decade old family-run store, which was a recipient of Stewards of Intangible Cultural Heritage Award in 2020.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Guan Hoe Soon
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eIndulge in delectable dishes like \u003ci\u003eayam buah keluak\u003c/i\u003e (chicken with black nut gravy),\u003ci\u003e ikan assam pedas\u003c/i\u003e (fish in a sour and spicy tamarind gravy) and \u003ci\u003eotak-otak\u003c/i\u003e (grilled fish cake with coconut milk and spices), at Singapore’s oldest Peranakan eatery.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Big Short Coffee
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eAt Big Short Coffee, coffees are crafted with scientific precision and cocktail creativity, featuring a rotating menu that changes every few months.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Birds of Paradise Gelato Boutique
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eThe ideal dessert pitstop, this Michelin-recommended local gelato brand serves up a range of unique, botanically-inspired flavours, from white chrysanthemum to vanilla fig.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: The Original Katong Laksa
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDig into this savoury home-grown noodle dish, with a broth made from coconut milk and ingredients like\u0026nbsp;cockles, prawns and fishcake.\u003c/p\u003e\r \u003cp\u003eThe version at Katong can\u0026nbsp;be easily slurped up with a spoon - no chopsticks needed!\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Old Bibik’s Peranakan Kitchen
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eFrom humble hawker beginnings in 2009, Old Bibik Peranakan Kitchen is a Joo Chiat gem serving vibrant, MSG-free Peranakan dishes rich in heritage and hearty flavours.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Hotel Indigo
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eImmerse in the local Peranakan culture at the quaint\u0026nbsp;Hotel Indigo, which fuses retro décor with modern swank.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Santa Grand Hotel
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eHoused in a building that embodies Chinese Baroque architecture, this hotel offers the best of both worlds, with its charming heritage and modern amenities.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 21
tiles.description: An inspiring blend of hip meets heritage, Chinatown is home to trendy eateries, buzzing watering holes and old-school charm.

tiles.title: Highlight 22
tiles.description: Skyscrapers and colonial buildings sit side by side in the Civic District, home to some of the island's finest museums and art galleries.

tiles.title: Highlight 23
tiles.description: Discover things to do in the Dempsey enclave, which covers the Dempsey, Minden, and Loewen clusters. Our guide covers unique shopping spots and what to eat at restaurants on Dempsey.

tiles.title: Highlight 24
tiles.description: Timeless tradition and bold new cultures come together on the streets of Kampong Gelam, where street art and trendy hangouts sit alongside traditional landmarks.

tiles.title: Highlight 25
tiles.description: Walk the streets of Little India, and discover a harmonious blend of age-old tradition, cutting edge architecture and shops selling traditional garments and intricate jewellery.

tiles.title: Highlight 26
tiles.description: Ignite your love for nature with the majestic animals, nature-themed attractions and lush greenery at Mandai.

tiles.title: Highlight 27
tiles.description: With its soaring skyscrapers and gorgeous skyline, the Marina Bay we see today is made up of 38 hectares of reclaimed land.

tiles.title: Highlight 28
tiles.description: Orchard Road is the beating heart of Singapore. From luxury shopping to subculture hangouts, there’s a new surprise waiting for you at every corner. Go where your heart takes you and experience the hottest attractions around. Or, take a look at our curated itineraries to find your place in Singapore’s busiest and most iconic street.

tiles.title: Highlight 29
tiles.description: Endless discovery awaits you with Sentosa's golden beaches, tranquil getaways and thrilling theme parks.

tiles.title: Highlight 30
tiles.description: From delectable food to buzzing nightlife, the Singapore River's trio of quays are bound to deliver a wave of exciting experiences.

contentLines: Singapore's Colorful Shophouses Along Koon Seng Road
Colourful Shophouses along Koon Seng Road
Colourful Stories From The Past

This once historic enclave whispers tales of the past, with the Peranakan inhabitants living here up till the 1970s. Admire the fusion of Chinese, Malay, and European influences, offering a glimpse into the unique identity of this cherished community. Peranakans are the descendants of Chinese or Indian immigrants who married indigenous people from the Malay Archipelago in the 15th century. In Singapore, their legacy is best seen in this area.
Architecture buffs should keep their eyes for intricate details, such as the
(swinging doors) and tiles adorned with floral motifs. Peer at the five-foot way — a roofed continuous walkway — for elaborate motifs and traditional Peranakan architecture.

Looking to snap a few photos? Be sure to come in an outfit that matches the candy-coloured hues of these iconic shophouses. Remember to be mindful and maintain a respectful volume while capturing memories amidst these charming residential homes.

contentLines: The Intan | Peranakan Home Museum in Singapore
A Showcase of Vibrant Culture

The Intan's collection is a proud display of Peranakan craftsmanship. Find over 5,000 Peranakan objects that are rich in history, from tiffin carriers, detailed embroidery to intricate beadwork shoes.
A Collection of Peranakan Stories

Experience a guided tour with owner and curator Alvin Yapp, who'll be happy to regale you with fascinating stories. Deep dive into the rich culture and be transported into the history, traditions & heritage and all things Peranakan!
A Trove of Mementos and Gifts
Seasonal rice dumplings, traditional coffee mugs and other traditional wares make for the perfect mementos to bring home.

contentLines: Kim Choo Kueh Chang | Peranakan Heritage
Scrumptious Peranakan Treats
Dig into savoury dumplings, traditional kueh (bite-sized snacks) and other Peranakan delights. Their Nyonya rice dumplings, which come in many flavours, are a must try.

This family-owned business taps on generations of recipes, knowledge, and techniques to create their iconic wares and flavourful eats. Besides that, Kim Choo Kueh Chang also offers workshops on beading, cooking and more, that will teach you the basics of Peranakan craftsmanship.

This Peranakan shophouse also doubles up as a Singapore Visitor Centre for the Katong-Joo Chiat precinct. You can get resources to help you navigate the neighbourhood, purchase tickets to attractions and tours, or pick up a souvenir.

contentLines: Eurasian Heritage Gallery | Community & Traditions

This charming building houses three distinct galleries that trace the rich heritage of Singapore's Eurasian community. The Eurasian community is one of Singapore’s smallest, but also one of its earliest. Known for their hybrid traditions of East and West, their Asian and European origins can be traced to some of the region’s oldest colonial settlements, such as Malacca, Penang, Goa, Macau and Ceylon (now Sri Lanka).
Sample Eurasian Culture On A Plate
Quentin's Eurasian Restaurant on the ground floor serves up authentic Eurasian food. Try the super-spicy Devil’s Curry or the traditional sugee cake, a nutty cake made from semolina and almonds.
Learn about Prominent Personalities
Learn more about the notable individuals from the community, from Olympic gold medallist Joseph Schooling to pioneering politicians like Benjamin Sheares.

little-india.name: Little India
little-india.title: Little India in Singapore

tiles.title: Sri Veerakaliamman Temple
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eBuilt by Indian pioneers living in the Serangoon district in the 19th century, this gorgeous place of worship is dedicated to Kali the Hindu goddess and destroyer of evil.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Indian Heritage Centre
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eIndian Heritage Centre\u0027s galleries and artefacts tell the enthralling story of Singapore\u0027s Indian community. The venue\u0026nbsp;also houses a Singapore Visitor Centre where you can pick up handy information.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Former House of Tan Teng Niah
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eBuilt in 1900, the\u0026nbsp;former house of Tan Teng Niah is a 2-storey villa with rainbow-hued exteriors that make for the perfect photo opportunity.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Tea \u0026 Tiffin: Cultural \u0026 Food Tour of Little India
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDiscover the tale of our country\u0027s Indian pioneers, tastes of tradition and our evolving cityscape on this vibrant and colourful tour with the masterful guides from Culture Curious.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Mustafa Centre
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eNo trip to Little India is complete without a visit to this massive department store, which sells everything from jewelry to groceries and electronics.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Jothi Store and Flower Shop
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eBesides flower garlands and prayer items sold for religious occasions, this store is filled with a range of traditional Indian beauty products, homeware, kitchenware and other colourful souvenirs.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Little India Arcade
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eA bustling area filled with an array of boutique shops and eateries. Discover henna art at Selvi\u0027s Beauty Salon, browse the goods at Gokulam Jewels and Craft, and indulge in dishes from Apolo\u0027s Food Village.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Haniffa
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eOriginally specialising in\u0026nbsp;\u003ci\u003esaris\u0026nbsp;\u003c/i\u003eand textiles when it opened in 1962, this traditional merchant now sells a variety of jewellery, electronics and other goods.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Tekka Centre
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eTekka Centre is Singapore’s largest indoor ‘wet’ market, selling an incredible array of fresh produce, aromatic spices and dried goods.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Banana Leaf Apolo
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eLocated along\u0026nbsp;Race Course Road, Banana Leaf Apolo is popular for its spread of delicious South Indian food. Be sure to sample the famous local delicacy, fish head curry on banana leaf.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Bismillah Biryani
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eA six-time Michelin Bib Gourmand Award Winner, this heritage restaurant doles out aromatic portions of authentic\u0026nbsp;\u003ci\u003edum biryani,\u0026nbsp;\u003c/i\u003ea traditional rice dish.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Olibier Rooftop Bar
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eKick back, relax with a cold beer or craft cocktails and enjoy the view at this laid-back rooftop bar. Expect chill tunes from live DJ sets and even a roving fortune teller on occasion.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Podi \u0026 Poriyal
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eWant to enjoy a slice of South India? Head over to Podi \u0026amp; Poriyal to check out its\u0026nbsp;vegetarian fare, innovative\u0026nbsp;cocktails and Indian snacks.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Hilton Garden Inn Singapore Serangoon
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eLocated at the heart of Little India, Hilton Garden Inn Singapore Serangoon is within walking distance from great shopping options like Mustafa Centre and Bugis Street.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Wanderlust
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eHoused in a heritage 1920s-styled building, Wanderlust is a boutique hotel near Little India and Bugis train stations, with uniquely themed rooms.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 16
tiles.description: An inspiring blend of hip meets heritage, Chinatown is home to trendy eateries, buzzing watering holes and old-school charm.

tiles.title: Highlight 17
tiles.description: Skyscrapers and colonial buildings sit side by side in the Civic District, home to some of the island's finest museums and art galleries.

tiles.title: Highlight 18
tiles.description: Discover things to do in the Dempsey enclave, which covers the Dempsey, Minden, and Loewen clusters. Our guide covers unique shopping spots and what to eat at restaurants on Dempsey.

tiles.title: Highlight 19
tiles.description: Timeless tradition and bold new cultures come together on the streets of Kampong Gelam, where street art and trendy hangouts sit alongside traditional landmarks.

tiles.title: Highlight 20
tiles.description: Home to Peranakan culture in Singapore, Katong-Joo Chiat is filled with local flavours, boutique cafes, and charming heritage shophouses.

tiles.title: Highlight 21
tiles.description: Ignite your love for nature with the majestic animals, nature-themed attractions and lush greenery at Mandai.

tiles.title: Highlight 22
tiles.description: With its soaring skyscrapers and gorgeous skyline, the Marina Bay we see today is made up of 38 hectares of reclaimed land.

tiles.title: Highlight 23
tiles.description: Orchard Road is the beating heart of Singapore. From luxury shopping to subculture hangouts, there’s a new surprise waiting for you at every corner. Go where your heart takes you and experience the hottest attractions around. Or, take a look at our curated itineraries to find your place in Singapore’s busiest and most iconic street.

tiles.title: Highlight 24
tiles.description: Endless discovery awaits you with Sentosa's golden beaches, tranquil getaways and thrilling theme parks.

tiles.title: Highlight 25
tiles.description: From delectable food to buzzing nightlife, the Singapore River's trio of quays are bound to deliver a wave of exciting experiences.

contentLines: Indian Heritage Centre & Museum in Singapore
Traditional Charm with a Modern Shine
A mix of traditional Indian design and modernity, the building's facade shines in the day and glows like a lantern at night.
A Celebration of Indian and South Asian History

From traditional garb, jewellery to ceramics, the heritage centre's galleries showcase the diversity and beauty of Indian culture. Discover over 400 artefacts on display at the museum, with more than half donated by or on loan from the community.
Diverse Themes and Artefacts

Experience the rich heritage of Indian culture at our gallery, divided into five captivating themes. Trace the journey of South Asian migration from the 19th to the 21st century, highlighting early interactions with Southeast Asia. Explore the profound contributions of Indian pioneers, including Mahatma Gandhi, and witness the pivotal role of Indians in shaping Singapore's history from the late 1950s to the 1980s.

contentLines: Sri Veeramakaliamman | Hindu Temple in Singapore
Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple

The temple's majestic gopuram or grand tower entrance is adorned with the figures of Hindu deities, while its interior is filled with majestic statues of the goddess Kali. With its colourful and intricate statues and detailing, the temple remains one of the most spectacular places of worship in Singapore.
A Landmark Rich in History
Formerly a shrine that was erected as early as 1855 by Indian pioneers, the temple has a rich history. Refugees who hid here during World War II air raids were left remarkably unscathed.
A Place of Faith and Worship
A popular landmark with travellers, feel free to snap pictures as remembrance of this colorful culture, but do be considerate of the temple's worshippers while visiting.

contentLines: Former House of Tan Teng Niah in Singapore | A Rich Heritage
Former House of Tan Teng Niah
History and Architectural Artistry

Once owned by a prominent Chinese businessman who owned factories in the neighbourhood, this colourful, two-storey bungalow is a must-visit for history buffs looking to admire both European and Chinese styles of architecture. Keep your eyes peeled for intricate details like the gilded Chinese calligraphy and bamboo-tiled roof.
Preserving Little India's History

Currently the last surviving Chinese villa in Little India, the former house of Tan Teng Niah offers a glimpse into the area's vibrant past, where Chinese businesses thrived alongside cattle herders, kilns, and rattan businesses.
When you're done snapping photos of the villa, head to surrounding streets like Hindoo Road, Bebilios Lane and Clive Street to explore the neighbourhood where murals and street arts are abound!

marina-bay.title: Marina Bay Singapore

tiles.title: Merlion Park
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eYour visit to Singapore isn\u0027t complete unless you\u0027ve snapped a photo with this iconic landmark! Located at Merlion Park, this majestic icon symbolises our nation\u0027s rich history as both fishing village and Lion City.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Esplanade - Theatres on The Bay
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eFrom rock music to ballet and theatre, this beloved art centre is home to an array of world-class performances and productions.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Gardens By The Bay
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eNature’s beauty is unveiled with Gardens by the Bay’s surreal sights, paradisal spaces and lush greenery.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Singapore Flyer
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eSee the world from a brand new perspective at the Singapore Flyer. Asia\u0027s largest observation wheel stands 165 metres above ground, with cabins that offer stunning views of the city.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Marina Barrage
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eBoth a water source and a popular haunt for local families, this charming spot boasts wide open spaces that are perfect for picnicking and kite-flying.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Marina Bay Sands
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eLive the high life at this iconic resort, with luxury accommodation, upscale shopping and an infinity pool that boasts unparalleled views of the city.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: ArtScience Museum
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eShaped like a lotus flower, this museum is where art meets tech. Step into dreamy digital worlds or explore mind-bending exhibitions. Kids love it, and so do adults.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eWith over 170 luxury brands – from Tiffany \u0026amp; Co to Acne Studio\u0027s first-in-Asia store – The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands is a great place to indulge in a bout of retail therapy.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Millenia Walk
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eFrom luxury brands to tech gadgets, Millenia Walk boasts a smorgasbord of diverse shopping opportunities.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Suntec City Mall
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eOne of Singapore\u0027s largest malls, this sprawling space is home to something for the entire family, from watches and beauty products to toys for the little ones.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Esplanade Mall
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDiscover the Esplanade Mall\u0027s diverse retail scene, offering a variety of stores from music to boutiques to suit your taste.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Republic Bar
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eImbibe on a liquid journey with a narrative of cocktails devoted to the 1960s at the award-winning Republic Bar.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: LeVeL 33
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eEnjoy a mug of artisanal beer and an unforgettable view at\u0026nbsp;LeVeL 33, the world\u0027s highest microbrewery.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Waku Ghin
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eHelmed by Tetsuya Wakuda, this two-Michelin-starred restaurant serves up\u0026nbsp;\u003ci\u003eomakase\u0026nbsp;\u003c/i\u003e(chef-selected) style meals made with immaculate craftsmanship and exquisite produce.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Labyrinth
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eThe brainchild of chef-owner LG Han, this Michelin-starred restaurant elevates local flavours with whimsical modern twists.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Kok Kee Wonton Noodles (MBS outlet)
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDig into oodles of noodles and enjoy a beloved hawker staple at this popular restaurant.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Satay by the Bay
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eFeast your senses at Satay by the Bay, where the aroma of satay and hawker favourites meet the breathtaking Marina Bay views and lush Gardens by the Bay scenery\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Marguerite
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eA feast for the senses, this Michelin-starred restaurant is located amid the lush beauty of Gardens by the Bay, and boasts equally stunning interiors.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: MO Bar
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eWith a breathtaking view of the skyline and delicious cocktails, a visit to MO Bar promises to be a heady experience.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Marina Bay Sands
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eIndulge in high-end amenities and unparalleled service at Marina Bay Sands, where you will find an infinity pool and an observation deck overlooking the city\u0027s skyline.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: The Fullerton Bay Hotel
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eThe Fullerton Bay Hotel Singapore promises you a luxurious stay, with a panoramic sweep of the Marina Bay waterfront.\u003cb\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\r \u003c/b\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 22
tiles.description: An inspiring blend of hip meets heritage, Chinatown is home to trendy eateries, buzzing watering holes and old-school charm.

tiles.title: Highlight 23
tiles.description: Skyscrapers and colonial buildings sit side by side in the Civic District, home to some of the island's finest museums and art galleries.

tiles.title: Highlight 24
tiles.description: Discover things to do in the Dempsey enclave, which covers the Dempsey, Minden, and Loewen clusters. Our guide covers unique shopping spots and what to eat at restaurants on Dempsey.

tiles.title: Highlight 25
tiles.description: Timeless tradition and bold new cultures come together on the streets of Kampong Gelam, where street art and trendy hangouts sit alongside traditional landmarks.

tiles.title: Highlight 26
tiles.description: Home to Peranakan culture in Singapore, Katong-Joo Chiat is filled with local flavours, boutique cafes, and charming heritage shophouses.

tiles.title: Highlight 27
tiles.description: Walk the streets of Little India, and discover a harmonious blend of age-old tradition, cutting edge architecture and shops selling traditional garments and intricate jewellery.

tiles.title: Highlight 28
tiles.description: Ignite your love for nature with the majestic animals, nature-themed attractions and lush greenery at Mandai.

tiles.title: Highlight 29
tiles.description: Orchard Road is the beating heart of Singapore. From luxury shopping to subculture hangouts, there’s a new surprise waiting for you at every corner. Go where your heart takes you and experience the hottest attractions around. Or, take a look at our curated itineraries to find your place in Singapore’s busiest and most iconic street.

tiles.title: Highlight 30
tiles.description: Endless discovery awaits you with Sentosa's golden beaches, tranquil getaways and thrilling theme parks.

tiles.title: Highlight 31
tiles.description: From delectable food to buzzing nightlife, the Singapore River's trio of quays are bound to deliver a wave of exciting experiences.

contentLines: Gardens by the Bay Singapore | Sky Garden & Light Show
A Space Where Nature Blooms

The beauty of nature beckons visitors to the Flower Dome in Bay South Gardens. Covering 1.28 hectares and home to plants and flowers from five continents, this verdant space broke the Guinness World Record as the World’s Largest Glass Greenhouse in 2015. From the Flower Dome, you can take a quick walk to the Cloud Forest to enjoy one of the world's tallest indoor waterfalls.

These iconic structures are home to vertical gardens and come to life in a glorious spectacle of light and sound after dusk. You can choose to scale the OCBC Skyway, an aerial walkway suspended between two Supertrees. The Supertrees also collect rainwater, generate solar power and act as venting ducts for the park’s conservatories. Don’t miss out on the Garden Rhapsody, a dazzling light show happening daily.
Home to over 200 sculptures, from unique stainless steel flower sculptures to recycled trash sculptures, whether you’re a nature lover, or art enthusiast, there’s something for everyone.

contentLines: Marina Bay Sands Singapore | Resort, SkyPark & Shopping

Soak in spectacular views with a 360 vista from the Sands SkyPark Observation Deck®. Or enjoy the breath-taking experience of swimming in the world’s largest infinity swimming pool while overlooking the horizon.
Where Art and Science Collide

The ArtScience Museum is home to a fascinating array of exhibitions that explore the intersections of art, culture and technology. This lotus-inspired museum is dubbed the welcoming hand of Singapore on the Marina Bay waterfront. Don’t forget to catch the Spectra – A Light & Water Show, a free nightly outdoor 15-minute extravaganza happening on selected days of the week.

At Marina Bay Sands, world-class dining and shopping experiences await. Discover over 170 premium brands at The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands®, home to flagship stores like Tiffany & Co., Louis Vuitton, Chanel and more. Complete your visit with a meal at celebrity chef restaurants, including Waku Ghin and CUT by Wolfgang Puck, for a taste of luxury in the heart of Singapore.

contentLines: Merlion Park Singapore | A Must-Visit Spot

With a head of a lion and a body of a fish, this beloved symbol has inspired myriad works of art and poetry. The Merlion’s fish-like body symbolises Singapore’s origins as a fishing village, known as Temasek—a name which comes from same root as the word
(lake in Malay). The statue’s head represents the city’s original name of Singapura (lion city in Sanskrit).
The Story Behind the Statue

Spouting water from its mouth, the Merlion statue stands at 8.6 metres and weighs 70 tonnes. Originally located at the mouth of the Singapore River, it was built by local craftsman Lim Nang Seng, designed by Kwan Sai Kheong, and unveiled on 15 September 1972 by then-Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew.

With the completion of Esplanade Bridge in 1997, the statue could no longer be viewed clearly from the waterfront and was relocated to the Merlion Park, which stands in front of Fullerton Hotel and overlooking Marina Bay.
Unwind Along the Singapore River

Whether you're looking to stroll along the river or catch a ride on a bumboat, the Singapore River is certainly worth exploring. From its origins as a fishing village known as Temasek, to its role as a trading port under the British Empire, the Lion City’s history has been inseparable from that of the Singapore River.

contentLines: Esplanade Theatres on the Bay | Singapore's Durian Building
Esplanade - Theatres on the Bay

Renowned for its striking exterior and thorny domes, Esplanade is shaped like a durian - the city's beloved tropical fruit. Marvel at its distinctive design, which is made with over 7,000 triangular aluminium sunshades.
From indie bands performing along the bay to award-winning stage productions, this venue is a paradise for lovers of drama and the performing arts.

Besides arts and culture, there are many places to eat at Esplanade. Check out bars, restaurants including the Michelin-starred Labyrinth, and street food at Makansutra Gluttons Bay - known for its hawker classics and lively open-air setting.

contentLines: A Sky-High Experience on the Singapore Ferris Wheel

A 30-minute ride in one of the Singapore Flyer's glass capsules offers 360-degree views. Feast your eyes on iconic and historical sights from Marina Bay to the Singapore River, such as Raffles Place and Merlion Park. With any luck, you’ll be able to spot landmarks up to 45km away, like Changi Airport, Sentosa Island and parts of Malaysia and Indonesia.
Besides its iconic observation wheel, the Singapore Flyer is also home to eateries, an art exhibition and the Time Capsule, a family-friendly multisensory activity that features Singapore's heritage.

Treat your loved one to a four-course dinner on the 165-metre-tall Singapore Flyer – the tallest revolving dining experience in the city. The 165 Sky Dining experience offers breathtaking night views of the Marina Bay skyline and is perfect for anniversaries, proposals, or any special celebration.

contentLines: Marina Barrage Singapore | Family Fun, Picnic, & More
Singapore's largest reservoir has a catchment area of 10,000 hectares, making it not just a crucial water source but also a prime place to kayak or canoe.
Fun with the entire Family
The greenery and wide-open space here makes for an idyllic place to picnic and fly a kite with your loved ones.
A Space for Sustainability

To learn more about Singapore's efforts to champion the environment, drop by the Sustainable Singapore Gallery. This educational space illustrates environmental and water issues through interactive multi-media displays, exhibits and games, with a guided tour available at the gallery.

contentLines: Emerald Hill Road | Shophouses, Restaurants, & Bars

Located amidst the hustle and bustle of Orchard Road, Emerald Hill was previously the site of a former nutmeg orchard, and subsequently developed into a fashionable abode for the wealthy Chinese and Straits-Chinese merchants.
The Chinese Baroque shophouses that line the gentle slope of Emerald Hill make for the perfect photo opportunity.
Whether you're in the mood for tapas or Peranakan-inspired cocktails, the bars along Emerald Hill make great spots to unwind.

contentLines: Design Orchard | One-Stop Shop for All Things Local
From exquisite scents and bold fashion to sophisticated homeware and playful souvenirs, you're bound to find a treasure to call your own at Design Orchard.
More than just a shopping space, Design Orchard is an incubator for some of Singapore's most promising talents and brands. Check out the sprawling showcase of over 90 local designers and brands.
Head up to the rooftop amphitheatre to be surrounded by lush gardens, grab a cup of coffee from the rooftop café and take in the sights and sounds of the bustling Orchard Road.

sentosa-island.name: Sentosa Island
sentosa-island.title: Sentosa Singapore: Top Things to Do on Sentosa Island

tiles.title: Harry Potter: Visions of Magic
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eExplore the mysterious corners of the wizarding world through Harry Potter: Visions of Magic, an interactive art experience inspired by places in the novels and film series.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Resorts World™ Sentosa
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eFrom underwater wonders to live events and fine dining, Resorts World™\u0026nbsp;Sentosa is full of excitement and enchantment.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Sensoryscape
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eEmbark on a sensory journey from Sentosa\u0027s lush ridges to its vibrant reefs, in this day-to-night experience.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: The Palawan @Sentosa
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eThis beach wonderland promises fun for all! Explore Asia’s first indoor gamified electric go-kart circuit, Singapore’s only floating aqua park, an 18-hole mini-golf course, beach clubs, iconic food trucks and more.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Singapore Cable Car
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eTravel to and from Sentosa in style, and discover spectacular views aboard the Singapore Cable Car ride.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: AltitudeX Singapore
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eFeel the rush of the wind through your head and the adrenaline through your veins at the world\u0027s largest wind tunnel for indoor skydiving.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: SkyPark Sentosa
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eTest your mettle as you hurtle through the air with SkyPark Sentosa\u0027s bungee jump and other high-flying attractions.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Mega Adventure Park
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eRide tandem with your little daredevils on the zipline, trampolines and obstacle courses at this adventure park.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: SentoSights – Sentosa Naturalist Night Adventure
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDiscover the sights and sounds of the rainforest after dark, with this nocturnal jaunt on Sentosa\u0027s wild side.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: SentoSights – Introduction to Birdwatching
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003ePick up the basics of birdwatching and admire the island\u0027s feathered inhabitants with this fascinating foray into nature.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: LEGO® Certified Store
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eSelling all things LEGO, Bricks World carries a wide range of LEGO products, from figurines to car models!\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Hershey’s Chocolate World Singapore
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eBring home a sweet gift at Hershey’s Chocolate World, from Hershey’s, to Reese’s and Twizzlers.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Jasons The Gourmet Grocer
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eChoose from a wide selection of groceries and epicurean brands at Jasons, a gourmet shopping paradise.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Tipsy Unicorn Beach Club
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eWith its pastel-hued decor and tasty cocktails, this bar and beach club is a great place to unwind.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: FOC by the Beach
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eKick back, indulge in delicious Mediterranean eats and sip on Sangrias at this beachside restaurant.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Good Old Days Food Court
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eIndulge in laksa, hokkien mee or other delicious local eats at this halal-certified food court.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Casserole
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eMeat-alternatives, vegan eat and vegetarian fare takes front and centre stage here, with a menu inspired by both Asian and Western cuisine.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Quentin\u0027s Eurasian Restaurant
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eFrom fiery curry\u0026nbsp;\u003ci\u003edebal\u0026nbsp;\u003c/i\u003eto hearty cod fritters and roasted pork belly, this restaurant is famous for authentic Eurasian fare.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: IMAMURA
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eThe brainchild of Michelin-starred chef Hirofumi Imamura, this restaurant\u0027s seasonal menu will delight your senses.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Ocean Restaurant
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDiscover what it\u0027s like to dine beneath the deep blue sea, as you dine alongside majestic sea creatures like sharks and manta rays.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Amara Sanctuary Sentosa
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eNestled within lush confines, Amara Sanctuary Sentosa has won numerous awards for its conservation efforts. Housed in a colonial style building, it offers nine room types.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Capella Singapore
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eLuxury awaits at the Capella Singapore. Find tranquility in a tropical oasis, with gourmet restaurants to choose from.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 23
tiles.description: An inspiring blend of hip meets heritage, Chinatown is home to trendy eateries, buzzing watering holes and old-school charm.

tiles.title: Highlight 24
tiles.description: Skyscrapers and colonial buildings sit side by side in the Civic District, home to some of the island's finest museums and art galleries.

tiles.title: Highlight 25
tiles.description: Discover things to do in the Dempsey enclave, which covers the Dempsey, Minden, and Loewen clusters. Our guide covers unique shopping spots and what to eat at restaurants on Dempsey.

tiles.title: Highlight 26
tiles.description: Timeless tradition and bold new cultures come together on the streets of Kampong Gelam, where street art and trendy hangouts sit alongside traditional landmarks.

tiles.title: Highlight 27
tiles.description: Home to Peranakan culture in Singapore, Katong-Joo Chiat is filled with local flavours, boutique cafes, and charming heritage shophouses.

tiles.title: Highlight 28
tiles.description: Walk the streets of Little India, and discover a harmonious blend of age-old tradition, cutting edge architecture and shops selling traditional garments and intricate jewellery.

tiles.title: Highlight 29
tiles.description: Ignite your love for nature with the majestic animals, nature-themed attractions and lush greenery at Mandai.

tiles.title: Highlight 30
tiles.description: With its soaring skyscrapers and gorgeous skyline, the Marina Bay we see today is made up of 38 hectares of reclaimed land.

tiles.title: Highlight 31
tiles.description: Orchard Road is the beating heart of Singapore. From luxury shopping to subculture hangouts, there’s a new surprise waiting for you at every corner. Go where your heart takes you and experience the hottest attractions around. Or, take a look at our curated itineraries to find your place in Singapore’s busiest and most iconic street.

tiles.title: Highlight 32
tiles.description: From delectable food to buzzing nightlife, the Singapore River's trio of quays are bound to deliver a wave of exciting experiences.

tiles.title: Highlight 1
tiles.description: With historical shophouses, old world charm and bustling watering holes, Emerald Hill is a great place to kick back with a cocktail in hand. \r

tiles.title: Highlight 2
tiles.description: Your one-stop shop for all things local, Design Orchard boasts a trove of wares proudly made in Singapore. \r

tiles.title: Highlight 3
tiles.description: Built in 1900, the former house of Tan Teng Niah is a 2-storey villa with pastel-hued exteriors, and is the last surviving Chinese villa in Little India. \r

contentLines: Resort World Sentosa Singapore - A Luxury Escape to an Island
Fantastic Fun for the Family

Enter into the seven movie-themed zones at Universal Studios, filled with exhilarating rides and outdoor shows, and where beloved movie characters like Shrek and Elmo come to life. Journey to the ocean's depths at the Singapore Oceanarium, which houses over 40,000 marine animals across 120 species, and a dedicated Research and Learning Centre. You can also visit family-friendly attractions like Adventure Cove, where you can drift away on a lazy boat ride and snorkel with fishes.

Whether you're in the mood for a steak dinner or a shopping spree, the world-class restaurants and boutiques at Resorts World™ Sentosa are bound to deliver. Fill your stomachs after a day of fun on the island with a perfect dining experience, catering to every taste bud.

Choose from five-star hotels like Equarius Hotel, Hotel Michael, or Ocean Suites – each offering a distinct experience, from lush forest views to underwater rooms. Whether you're seeking a romantic escape or a family-friendly retreat, Resorts World Sentosa makes every stay unforgettable.

singapore-river.title: Singapore River

tiles.title: Kulnari Mystery Golf
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eHole in ones meets mysterious historical intrigue at Kulnari Mystery Golf, a charming blend of mini-golf course and escape room shenanigans.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Slingshot
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eYou don\u0027t even have to look to find this ride – Just listen for the screams of exhilaration. Strap in for a rush, this ride reaches speeds of 160 kilometres per hour!\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Zouk
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eHome to world-class DJs and nonstop party vibes, this legendary venue is a stalwart of Singapore\u0027s nightlife scene.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Asian Civilisations Museum
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eFrom the salvaged cargo of a Tang dynasty shipwreck to religious statues and ceramics, the Asian Civilisations Museum is a trove of the region\u0027s diverse cultures.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Evolve MMA
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eGet your gloves up – whether you\u0027re looking to pick up Muay Thai strikes or Brazilian Jiu Jitsu holds, Evolve MMA is a great place to get started.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Prestique Studio
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eBounce to your heart\u0027s content at Prestique Studio! Both fun and great for fitness, the unique workouts here get your heart rate up through the use of mini-trampolines.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Singapore River Cruise
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eCruise down the Singapore River, learn about our city\u0027s rich history and take in the gorgeous sights of our skyline. You can even enjoy dinner on the water while enjoying the experience.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Singapore Street Food and Night Tour
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eIt\u0027s not just our city lights that sparkle after dark – discover our city\u0027s UNESCO-awarded hawker culture on this three and-a-half hour long jaunt through Singapore\u0027s vibrant night life.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Clarke Quay Central
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eYou\u0027ll find fashion boutiques and stores selling a range of gifts, accessories and gadgets at this conveniently-located mall.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Clarke Quay Street Stalls
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eWith its bustling vibes and ever-changing lineup of trinkets, this is a great place to pick up a souvenir.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Riverside Point
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eShop for gifts and soak in the bustle along the riverside at this charming locale.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Offtrack
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eArt, food and music come together at Offtrack, an effortlessly cool bar that serves up Pan Asian cuisine, cocktails and live DJ sets.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Shabestan
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eFrom juicy beef kebabs to hearty Persian stews, the dishes at this eatery along the Singapore River are bound to get your mouth watering.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Jiak Kim House
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDiscover Singapore’s culinary heritage in a beautifully restored 1920s Singapore River warehouse. Savour bold Modern Asian dishes that celebrate the best of East and West.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Quay House
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eNestled in the heart of Boat Quay, Quay House honours its spice trading past with Asian tapas inspired by the Maritime Silk Route.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: 21 Carpenter
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eReimagined and restored by award-winning architects WOHA, this exquisite boutique hotel offers an unforgettable stay with its garden terrace and rooftop infinity pool.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: The Warehouse Hotel
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eGiving industrial design a new local spin, this boutique hotel is housed in a restored heritage building on the bank of the Singapore River.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 18
tiles.description: An inspiring blend of hip meets heritage, Chinatown is home to trendy eateries, buzzing watering holes and old-school charm.

tiles.title: Highlight 19
tiles.description: Skyscrapers and colonial buildings sit side by side in the Civic District, home to some of the island's finest museums and art galleries.

tiles.title: Highlight 20
tiles.description: Discover things to do in the Dempsey enclave, which covers the Dempsey, Minden, and Loewen clusters. Our guide covers unique shopping spots and what to eat at restaurants on Dempsey.

tiles.title: Highlight 21
tiles.description: Timeless tradition and bold new cultures come together on the streets of Kampong Gelam, where street art and trendy hangouts sit alongside traditional landmarks.

tiles.title: Highlight 22
tiles.description: Home to Peranakan culture in Singapore, Katong-Joo Chiat is filled with local flavours, boutique cafes, and charming heritage shophouses.

tiles.title: Highlight 23
tiles.description: Walk the streets of Little India, and discover a harmonious blend of age-old tradition, cutting edge architecture and shops selling traditional garments and intricate jewellery.

tiles.title: Highlight 24
tiles.description: Ignite your love for nature with the majestic animals, nature-themed attractions and lush greenery at Mandai.

tiles.title: Highlight 25
tiles.description: With its soaring skyscrapers and gorgeous skyline, the Marina Bay we see today is made up of 38 hectares of reclaimed land.

tiles.title: Highlight 26
tiles.description: Orchard Road is the beating heart of Singapore. From luxury shopping to subculture hangouts, there’s a new surprise waiting for you at every corner. Go where your heart takes you and experience the hottest attractions around. Or, take a look at our curated itineraries to find your place in Singapore’s busiest and most iconic street.

tiles.title: Highlight 27
tiles.description: Endless discovery awaits you with Sentosa's golden beaches, tranquil getaways and thrilling theme parks.

tiles.description: From street food to heritage dining haunts and Michelin-starred restaurants, embark on this food trail that will take your taste buds on a wild ride.

tiles.title: Highlight 2
tiles.description: Embark on a 2-day journey in Singapore, immersing yourself in a blend of cultural experiences, museum visits, attractions, through Singapore’s diverse cityscape.

tiles.title: Highlight 3
tiles.description: Find new ways to relax, rejuvenate and revitalise your body and spirit during your tropical vacation to the Lion City.

tiles.title: Highlight 4
tiles.description: In town for a while? Shop, eat, and play with this detailed itinerary and enjoy the best of Singapore.

tiles.title: Highlight 5
tiles.description: With a week to spare, discover how East meets West, nature and urban beauty intertwine, and the past meets present, with our guide to Singapore's most iconic spots.

tiles.title: Highlight 6
tiles.description: From unique local designers to some of the world’s largest global luxury brands, shopaholics are in for a treat.

tiles.title: Highlight 7
tiles.description: Whether you’re newly-married or on a wedding anniversary, Singapore is the perfect destination for couples in the mood for love.

tiles.title: Highlight 8
tiles.description: Explore top outdoor adventure activities in Singapore - from biking in Pulau Ubin, to kayaking along mangroves, hiking trails and luge rides. Perfect for nature lovers!

tiles.title: Highlight 9
tiles.description: What to see, food to eat, things to do, experiences that can’t be missed—here’s a guide to the best of Singapore that’s fit for all ages.

tiles.title: Highlight 10
tiles.description: Celebrate your hen party in one of the world's safest cities! Enjoy bachelorette trip ideas like spa, cocktails & nightlife for the perfect girls' getaway.

tiles.title: Highlight 11
tiles.description: Planning a Singapore solo trip opens up a world of freedom and discovery. Wander heritage neighbourhoods on your own, pause for reflection in tranquil gardens, or treat yourself to a Michelin-starred meal.

itinerary-4days.name: 4 Days in Singapore (Essential Explorer)
itinerary-4days.title: Explore Singapore in 4 Days: Ultimate Itinerary & Tours!

tiles.title: Highlight 1
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eStart your day with breakfast at this conserved area, where Malay royalty once resided, and is steeped in rich culture and history.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 2
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eWake your taste buds up with a classic Singapore-style breakfast, by dropping by Singapore Zam Zam Restaurant for prata (South Indian flatbread) and a side of curry.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 3
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eHead to Haji Lane —a hipster haunt littered with indie outlets that stock vintage clothing and knick-knacks—such as home and lifestyle store Hygge.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 4
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eCome midday, make your way to the Civic District. Pop by Raffles Hotel for lunch, known for its rich history and exquisite colonial architecture.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 5
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eExplore the timeless allure of Long Bar, renowned for being the birthplace of the legendary Singapore Sling cocktail.\u003cbr /\u003e\r \u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 6
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eThen, pay a visit to National Gallery Singapore to marvel at the world\u0027s largest public display of modern Southeast Asian art.\u003cbr\u003e\r \u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 7
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eJust before dinner, hop on a traditional bumboat by Singapore River Cruise and get to know the historic Singapore River.\u003cbr /\u003e\r \u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 8
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eArt, food and music come together at Offtrack, an effortlessly cool bar that serves up Pan Asian cuisine, cocktails and live DJ sets.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 9
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eA cocktail bar inspired by the birds of Singapore, PLUME serves up intriguing cocktails and appetisers.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 10
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eNestled in the East, with its rainbow-hued heritage shophouses, hip cafes and modern boutiques, this is one of Singapore’s most charming districts.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 11
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eIndulge in an old-school Singapore style breakfast with the fluffiest buns and thick spreads of homemade coconut kaya jam.\u003cbr /\u003e\r \u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 12
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eFrom stunning traditional wares and unique souvenirs, this beloved store is your one-stop shop for discovering the rich tapestry of Peranakan culture.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 13
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eOnce a Chinese immigrant enclave, today\u0027s Chinatown is a mix of old and new, with historic temples alongside award-winning bars and restaurants.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 14
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eVisit Maxwell Food Centre for local chicken rice from Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice, and grab a cold glass of sugarcane juice to quench your thirst.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 15
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eContinue by foot and discover Chinatown\u0027s rich culture and history at the Buddha Tooth Relic Temple.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 16
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eAn iconic district, immerse in cityscape views, stunning architecture and trendy dining spots.\u003cbr /\u003e\r \u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 17
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eWith over 170 luxury brands – from Tiffany \u0026amp; Co to Acne Studio\u0027s first-in-Asia store – The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands is a great place to indulge in a bout of retail therapy.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 18
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDig into a plate of chill crab – Singapore\u0027s most iconic seafood dish – and indulge in a variety of classic sharing dishes.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 19
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eEnjoy lush gardens, peace and tranquility at this 150-year-old green destination–which happens to be Singapore’s first UNESCO World Heritage Site.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 20
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDon’t miss the National Orchid Garden, home to the largest orchid display in the world with over 60,000 plants and orchids on display.\u003cbr\u003e\r \u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 21
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eBreak for brunch - located amidst the one-hectare Ginger Garden, this restaurant specialises in contemporary European cuisine.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 22
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eSwitch up the pace – head to Singapore’s major shopping district, where you’ll find a mix of high-end brands, local labels, and everything in between.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 23
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eExperience a curation of over 100 homegrown fashion and lifestyle labels, the largest one-stop destination to shop all things local.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 24
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eTantalise your tastebuds with Peranakan cuisine. This homegrown dining is famous for serving up authentic dishes, from dry laksa to aromatic curries.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 25
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eExplore Bugis, a district with a colorful past and is now known for its trendy stores. Find great bargains and more at Bugis Street Market.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 26
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eMake a beeline for the ethnic enclave Little India, and tuck into mouth-watering South Indian food such as popular local delicacy fish head curry at Banana Leaf Apolo.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 27
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eItching for more shopping options? Check out Mustafa Centre–a shopping complex that sells just about everything you can think of. Best of all, it’s open till late night.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 28
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eMake your way to the Northern area of Singapore to be enthralled by the abundance of flora and fauna in our world-class attractions.\u003cbr\u003e\r \u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 29
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eHome to over 3,500 birds, be immersed in naturalistic walk-through aviaries that reflect different habitats of the world.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 30
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eAlternatively, head to an award-winning wildlife park home to more than 2,400 animals across 300 species, and encounter free-roaming animals.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 31
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003ePlay, dine or enjoy a quick respite from your wildlife adventure, from the towering waterfall upon arrival to the interactive play areas.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 32
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eDig into a four-course dinner in Singapore\u0027s largest Tipi Tent and embark on a tram ride to discover the mysterious creatures of the night.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.title: Highlight 33
tiles.description: \u003cp\u003eFor your final stop, hop on over to the Night Safari. This park welcomes guests to the world’s first nocturnal safari experience with over 900 animals.\u003c/p\u003e\r

tiles.description: From street food to heritage dining haunts and Michelin-starred restaurants, embark on this food trail that will take your taste buds on a wild ride.
